title: Security and multi-tenancy
summary: Threat modelling for system design: authn/authz at scale, secrets, encryption at rest/in transit, tenant isolation models, audit trails.

units.title: Who can do what, to whose data
Protecting data and proving what happened

labs.title: Tenant-scoped data access and a weighted-fair noisy-neighbour limiter
Tamper-evident (hash-chained) audit log with per-tenant chains and anchors
Envelope encryption sketch: KEK/DEK, AAD, rewrap rotation, crypto-shredding

outcomes.text: Threat-model a feature in five minutes (assets, actors, trust boundaries, STRIDE-lite, ranked abuse cases) and turn the top threats into testable security requirements.

Decide where tokens are validated and where authorisation decisions are made (gateway, service, data layer), choose between RBAC, ABAC and relationship-based models, and state the revocation trade-off.
Prevent BOLA/IDOR and confused-deputy bugs structurally by authorising at the data layer, and explain 404 versus 403 for out-of-scope objects.
Implement a tenant-scoped data-access layer whose API shape makes cross-tenant reads and writes impossible (labs/a9/tenancy).

Choose between silo, pool and bridge/cell isolation for tenants of different sizes, and enforce the boundary with scoped repositories, row-level security (per-transaction variables) and composite keys.

Implement a per-tenant weighted-fair limiter with borrowing and a cap, size concurrency limits with Little's law, and explain why a global limit does not protect against noisy neighbours (labs/a9/tenancy).
Design secrets management (workload identity, dynamic short-lived credentials, rotation without downtime with dual-key windows) and keep secrets out of env vars, images and logs.
Explain which attacker each encryption layer defeats (TLS, mTLS, volume, TDE, application-level, tokenisation) and where verification and identity checks are required.
Explain envelope encryption and key hierarchies: KEK/DEK, AAD binding, DEK caching and KMS cost, rotation by re-wrapping, nonce limits, BYOK and crypto-shredding.

Implement a tamper-evident hash-chained audit log, state exactly which attacks the chain detects and which need an external anchor, and design the audit pipeline (what to log, separation of duties, retention, PII) (labs/a9/auditlog).
Map compliance frameworks (SOC 2, PCI DSS, GLBA/NCUA, FFIEC) onto concrete controls and evidence, and design data lifecycle, retention and just-in-time privileged access.
Implement an envelope-encryption sketch (KMS wrap/unwrap/rewrap, per-tenant DEKs, AAD, shredding) with the standard library (labs/a9/envelope).
Explain Zanzibar-style relationship-based access control: tuples, rewrites, usersets, consistency tokens and the new enemy problem.
Explain Merkle trees and transparency logs: inclusion and consistency proofs, domain separation, signed tree heads and witnesses.
